newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Post Bank restores one-tier management.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Post Bank restores one-tier management.

text.p: The state-owned Bulgarian Post Bank (BPB) on Friday restored its one-tier management system from a two-tier one in a bid to achieve greater operational flexibility, a bank's executive director said on Friday.
"The one tier-management system by a seven-member board of directors has been restored under today's decision of Post Bank shareholders," Vladimir Vladimirov told a news conference.

The two-tier management system, which involved an executive board and a supervisory board, has been introduced at the BPB at the beginning of last year to build up government control but was not necessary any longer, said Vladimirov.

The board of directors includes the Bank Consolidation Company (BCC), Bulgarian Posts, Bulgarian Telecommunication Company (BTC), the National Palace of Culture as legal entities and three executive directors.

The Bulgarian Posts and the Telecom Company were planning to raise their stakes into the bank's capital to strengthen the bank's role as a financial institution servicing posts and telecommunications, Vladimirov said.
The BCC, which manages state equity in local commercial banks, now holds 78.23 percent of Post Bank capital, which totals 2.421 billion levs. Bulgarian Posts and BTC hold 5.03 percent each.

BPB posted 344 million lev net profit for 1996 under local accountancy standarts against a 3.65 billion lev loss for 1995, bank balance sheet figures showed. The shareholders decided to set aside to reserves the whole net profit, Vladimirov said.
The bank had set aside provisions of 19.5 billion levs against its risk assets and had paid 260 million levs of taxes for last year.
The BPB capital to risk assets ratio stood at 11.2 percent at end-1996, Vladimirov said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
